11.t: Working with data: pressure and height
q: What is the air pressure at sea level?
What is the air pressure at the top of Mount Everest (about 9 km)?
About 31 kPa, less than a third of sea level.
Describe how air pressure changes with height.
It decreases as height increases, fastest near the ground and more slowly higher up.
Use particles to explain the pattern, and suggest why climbers on Everest often carry oxygen.
Higher up there are fewer air particles above pushing down and fewer in each breath, so pressure is lower. Each breath has far fewer oxygen particles, so climbers carry oxygen to get enough.
